scope: Real owned backend process crashes after loopback provider mutations, before response delivery or durable outcome recording

validation.cleanup: Passed: owned stack removed, 42 pre-existing containers restored, Colima stopped and generated Next files restored

assertions: Mock records the mutation and holds its HTTP response; the API observes exactly one prepared intent for the held key
Actual SIGKILL exit is verified and a different owned backend process restarts with the same database
Prepared intent remains without an invented outcome; raw submission stays sending while owner status requires recovery
Initial reads after restart acquire no provider tokens and perform no provider calls
Claims, managed head, journal, successful references and feedback equal the pre-crash snapshot
Two exact retries return 409; reloads and status reads add no provider calls or durable changes
Owner has no send/continue/feedback action; mobile layout, browser health and egress checks pass
Strict archives preserve three source versions/approvals/claims/submissions/originals and four previous feedback originals
Confirmation crash invents no receipt or feedback despite the mock recording confirmation
Main-crash prepared history also survives actual same-cluster database restore and retained byte verification; unrelated actors denied
limitations: Loopback mock results do not establish real provider idempotency or authorize replay
Before-I/O process-loss browser coverage, rejected-predecessor and remaining security/conformance checks remain
Ordinary Storage objects, independent-cluster role recovery, prior-year/unapproved restore, cancellation/expiry/deletion and retention generations remain
Unknown-operation reconciliation, legacy feedback backfill, HTTP/concurrency sizing and both immutable acceptance gates remain
All seven RF acceptance criteria pending; draft PR only, no production enablement, hosted database change, genuine provider effect or real AS data
